facts.value: No separate termination deadline; final wages follow the semi-monthly schedule in R.C. 4113.15(A): first-half wages by the 1st of the next month, second-half wages by the 15th
facts.summary: Ohio has no separate final-pay deadline; final wages are due on the regular semi-monthly schedule (first half of a month by the 1st of the next month, second half by the 15th).
facts.evidence_quote: (A) Every employer doing business in this state shall, on or before the first day of each month, pay all its employees the wages earned by them during the first half of the preceding month ending with the fifteenth day thereof, and shall, on or before the fifteenth day of each month, pay such employees the wages earned by them during the last half of the preceding calendar month.
facts.notes: R.C. 4113.15(A) applies to all employees whether or not separated (Catalyst Compliance reading).

facts.summary: Ohio basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $11.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Employers with annual gross receipts of $405,000 or more Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $11.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Employers with annual gross receipts under $405,000 Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 The minimum wage is adjusted annually based on a set formula
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Multiple rates listed by DOL (see quote): $11.00, $7.25 | Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Semi-monthly schedule: first-half wages by the 1st of the next month, second-half wages by the 15th
facts.summary: Ohio pay frequency rule: Semi-monthly schedule: first-half wages by the 1st of the next month, second-half wages by the 15th.
facts.evidence_quote: (A) Every employer doing business in this state shall, on or before the first day of each month, pay all its employees the wages earned by them during the first half of the preceding month ending with the fifteenth day thereof, and shall, on or before the fifteenth day of each month, pay such employees the wages earned by them during the last half of the preceding calendar month.
facts.notes: Section also says it does not prohibit daily or weekly payment.

facts.value: Yes: private employers must insure through the Ohio state insurance fund (BWC) or be BWC-approved self-insurers
facts.summary: Ohio is a monopolistic state: private employers pay workers' comp premiums into the state insurance fund or qualify as self-insurers.
facts.evidence_quote: every private employer and every publicly owned utility shall pay semiannually in the months of January and July into the state insurance fund the amount of annual premium the administrator of workers' compensation fixes for the employment or occupation of the employer
facts.notes: Self-insurance exception is in the same section (R.C. 4123.35(B)).
